description: Raw access to the registers of a Commodore 64 SID chip, emulated with ReSID, with three voices, a shared filter and a CV jack beside every register field

params.text: Sets the pitch of that voice, 54 semitones either side of C4, written into the chip's 16-bit frequency register
Sets the duty cycle of that voice's pulse waveform, 50% at the centre and reaching 0% and 100% at the ends, written as a 12-bit value
Switches the triangle waveform into that voice; picking more than one waveform at once does not mix them, the chip combines them into a single new shape
Switches the sawtooth waveform into that voice, and while it is on the chip ignores that voice's ring modulation
Switches the pulse waveform into that voice, its width taken from the PW knob and the PW input
Switches the noise waveform into that voice; the noise is clocked from that voice's own frequency, so the pitch controls set how bright it is
Runs the attack, decay and sustain of that voice's envelope while it is on, and the release when it goes off
Resets voice 1's oscillator every time voice 3's oscillator wraps round, which is hard sync
Resets voice 2's oscillator every time voice 1's oscillator wraps round, which is hard sync
Resets voice 3's oscillator every time voice 2's oscillator wraps round, which is hard sync
Ring modulates voice 1's triangle waveform against voice 3's oscillator; it changes nothing unless the triangle is on, and the sawtooth being on cancels it
Ring modulates voice 2's triangle waveform against voice 1's oscillator; it changes nothing unless the triangle is on, and the sawtooth being on cancels it
Ring modulates voice 3's triangle waveform against voice 2's oscillator; it changes nothing unless the triangle is on, and the sawtooth being on cancels it
Clears that voice's oscillator and holds it at zero, which silences the voice and forces its pulse output high until this goes off again
Sets the attack time of that voice's envelope, which the chip stores as one of 16 steps
Sets the decay time of that voice's envelope, which the chip stores as one of 16 steps
Sets the sustain level of that voice's envelope, which the chip stores as one of 16 steps
Sets the release time of that voice's envelope, which the chip stores as one of 16 steps
Routes that voice through the filter; a voice with this off goes straight to the output unfiltered
Routes the Aux input through the filter instead of straight to the output
Switches the filter's lowpass output on; the chip sums whichever of the three modes are on, so lowpass and highpass together make a notch
Switches the filter's bandpass output on; the chip sums whichever of the three modes are on
Switches the filter's highpass output on; the chip sums whichever of the three modes are on, so highpass and lowpass together make a notch
Cuts voice 3 out of the audio output, which frees it as a modulation source at the Osc and Env jacks
Sets the filter cutoff, written as an 11-bit value from 0 to 2047
Sets the filter resonance, which the chip stores as one of 16 steps
Sets the chip's master volume as one of 16 steps, applied to everything it puts out

inputs.text: Transposes that voice at one volt per octave, added to the Pitch knob, with no clamp of its own
Shifts the duty cycle of that voice's pulse waveform, ±5V covering the whole sweep, added to the PW knob and clamped at the ends
1V or more switches the triangle waveform into that voice; the voltage is added to the switch, so with the switch already on -1V or less switches it off again
1V or more switches the sawtooth waveform into that voice; the voltage is added to the switch, so with the switch already on -1V or less switches it off again
1V or more switches the pulse waveform into that voice; the voltage is added to the switch, so with the switch already on -1V or less switches it off again
1V or more switches the noise waveform into that voice; the voltage is added to the switch, so with the switch already on -1V or less switches it off again
1V or more opens that voice's envelope and anything below closes it; the voltage is added to the Gate switch, so with that switch on the voice stays open
1V or more resets voice 1's oscillator from voice 3's; the voltage is added to the Sync switch, so with that switch on -1V or less turns the sync off
1V or more resets voice 2's oscillator from voice 1's; the voltage is added to the Sync switch, so with that switch on -1V or less turns the sync off
1V or more resets voice 3's oscillator from voice 2's; the voltage is added to the Sync switch, so with that switch on -1V or less turns the sync off
1V or more ring modulates voice 1's triangle against voice 3's oscillator; the voltage is added to the RingMod switch, so -1V or less turns it off again
1V or more ring modulates voice 2's triangle against voice 1's oscillator; the voltage is added to the RingMod switch, so -1V or less turns it off again
1V or more ring modulates voice 3's triangle against voice 2's oscillator; the voltage is added to the RingMod switch, so -1V or less turns it off again
1V or more clears and holds that voice's oscillator; the voltage is added to the Test switch, so with that switch on -1V or less releases the oscillator
Lengthens that voice's attack, 0-10V covering the 16 steps, added to the Attack trimmer and clamped at the ends
Lengthens that voice's decay, 0-10V covering the 16 steps, added to the Decay trimmer and clamped at the ends
Raises that voice's sustain level, 0-10V covering the 16 steps, added to the Sustain trimmer and clamped at the ends
Lengthens that voice's release, 0-10V covering the 16 steps, added to the Release trimmer and clamped at the ends
1V or more routes that voice through the filter; the voltage is added to the switch, so with the switch on -1V or less takes the voice back out
1V or more routes the Aux input through the filter; the voltage is added to the Aux switch, so with that switch on -1V or less takes it back out
1V or more switches the filter's lowpass output on; the voltage is added to the LP switch, so with that switch on -1V or less switches it off
1V or more switches the filter's bandpass output on; the voltage is added to the BP switch, so with that switch on -1V or less switches it off
1V or more switches the filter's highpass output on; the voltage is added to the HP switch, so with that switch on -1V or less switches it off
1V or more cuts voice 3 out of the audio output; the voltage is added to the 3Off switch, so with that switch on -1V or less puts voice 3 back
Moves the filter cutoff, 0-10V covering the whole 0 to 2047 range, added to the CutOff knob and clamped at the ends
Raises the filter resonance, 0-10V covering the 16 steps, added to the Res knob and clamped at the ends
Changes the chip's master volume, 0-10V covering the 16 steps, added to the Volume knob and clamped at the ends
An external signal fed into the chip's audio path, ±5V taken as full scale, mixed in with the three voices and filtered only if the Aux switch is on
A rising edge here writes the current control and CV values into the chip's registers; with a cable patched the module's internal update clock is ignored

outputs.text: The chip's audio, all three voices and the Aux input together, each of them filtered or dry according to the filter switches
A 10V pulse 0.1ms long every time the chip's registers are written, whether the update came from the Clk input or from the internal clock
Voice 3's envelope, read back from the chip as an 8-bit register value and scaled to 0-10V, so it moves in 256 steps
Voice 3's oscillator, read back from the chip as an 8-bit register value and scaled to ±5V, so it moves in 256 steps

notes: every voice starts with its Gate switch off, so the module makes no sound until you turn a Gate switch on or send 1V or more to a Gate input
each control's value is added to the voltage at the jack beside it, so to drive a register from CV alone you have to turn that knob or switch fully off first
the registers are written only at the update rate, either the internal vertical-refresh clock or a rising edge at the Clk input, so a control you move does nothing until the next write
the small lamp beside each waveform, control, envelope and filter CV input shows the value that parameter has in the chip's registers, and it changes only when the registers are written
menu: Reset SID Chip — clears the emulated chip and the module's copy of its registers and starts it again
SID Model: MOS 6581, MOS 8580, MOS 8580 (Digi Boost) — picks which chip is emulated; the Digi Boost option holds the chip's audio input at full negative while the Aux jack is empty
CPU Clock: PAL (50Hz vsync), NTSC (60Hz vsync) — sets the emulated machine's clock and the register update rate with it, 985248Hz and 50Hz, or 1022727Hz and 60Hz
VSync Oversample: x1, x2, x4, x8, x16, No VSync — multiplies the internal register update rate; No VSync writes the registers on every audio sample instead
Sample Mode: Direct, Interpolate, Resample, Resample Fastmem — picks how the chip's output reaches the engine; Direct clocks the chip once per audio sample and reads it straight out
